transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because things at work have gotten... hard to ignore. The routing system at the warehouse, it’s not just a computer to me anymore. I know it’s tracking my moves, marking where I go, and sending messages through the scanners. It feels like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.
During this time, have you had a period where your mood felt unusually high or energized?
I don’t think so. I haven’t felt unusually high or energized, not like that. If anything, I’ve just been worn down and on edge.
Have you had any recent seizures, head injuries, or other neurological illness?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t had any seizures or head injuries recently. I’m not aware of any neurological illness.
Have you heard voices or other sounds that other people could not hear?

Yes. I hear voices when nobody’s around. Like when I’m sitting in my garage and everything’s shut off, I can hear dispatch voices clear as day calling my operator number. They say I’m dangerous, or that security is coming for me. It’s... it sounds real to me.
About how long have the voices and the belief that the system is tracking you been going on?
It’s been about a year and eight months now. The voices and the thing with the scanners tracking me… it’s been going on that long.
During this time, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yes. It’s been more than two weeks… a lot more. The depression’s been hanging over me for about two years and a month, since not long after the schedule change started wearing me down. Most days it’s just there.
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices or felt the system was tracking you, but you were not depressed during that time?

Yes. There was a stretch where I wasn’t as down as usual. My mood had eased up some, and I was eating a little more, talking a little more. But even then, for several weeks, I was still hearing dispatch call my number, and I still believed the routing system was tracking me.
Have other people told you that your speech becomes hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense?
I’m not really sure. Nobody’s told me that directly, at least not that I remember. I know sometimes I lose my train of thought, but I don’t know if it sounds hard to follow to other people.
Have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?

Yes. My wife says I barely answer her anymore. I guess I don’t talk much unless I have to. Most days I just sit at the kitchen table with my coffee, staring at it, and I don’t really get started on anything. She says my face looks flat too.
During times when the voices or the feeling of being tracked were happening, did you ever have at least two weeks with no depression at all?

Not no depression at all, I don’t think. It had eased up some—I was eating a little more and talking a little more—but I wasn’t completely fine. And even then, for several weeks, I was still hearing dispatch call my number and still felt like the routing system was tracking me.
At any point since the voices started, was there ever a time when you heard them while your depression was absent?

I don’t think it was completely absent. There was a stretch where my mood had eased up some—I was eating a little more, talking a little more—but for several weeks I was still hearing dispatch call my number, and I still felt like the routing system was tracking me.
Since the voices and the feeling of being tracked began, has depression been present for most of that time?

Yes. Most of the time, I’ve still been depressed. Even when the warehouse stuff got a little quieter for a while, I was still down and empty. I couldn’t get myself back to things I used to care about, like fishing or woodworking, or even sitting down for family meals.
